biggest_catch: Applying to freelance jobs requires a paid Behance Pro subscription — only full-time/contract roles are free to apply.
catches: Freelance proposals require Behance Pro (paid) — the free path covers only full-time/contract roles.
Listings skew toward employer jobs, not gig work; winning is competitive and never guaranteed.
Pay is set per listing by each employer — Behance publishes no fixed pay range.
Requires a strong portfolio to be competitive.

c1.evidence: Behance's own blog describes the rebuilt job board: 'Search, sort, and filter freelance and full-time opportunities', 'Browse and apply to full-time roles for free', and 'Get job alerts: set your criteria once and you'll receive emails about new listings as they come in' — a real, public deal-sourcing channel.

c2.evidence: Official pages publish no fixed pay range — pay is set per listing; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: build profile, browse/filter the job board, save jobs, apply inline, or set job alerts.

c4.evidence: Browsing and applying to full-time roles is free; freelance proposals require paid Behance Pro (optional, not required for the free route).

eligibility: Designers and creative professionals with a portfolio; free path covers full-time/contract roles.
notes: Scenario: design jobs board. Behance's rebuilt job board unifies freelance and full-time creative roles with inline applications and email job alerts — a standing deal source for designers. Free to browse and apply for full-time roles; freelance proposals need Behance Pro. Pay is per-listing and variable — never guaranteed.

steps: Build or polish your Behance profile and portfolio.
Browse the rebuilt Behance job board: filter freelance vs full-time, location, and salary range.
Save promising listings; set job alerts to get new matches by email.
Apply inline to full-time roles for free (freelance proposals require paid Behance Pro).
Get hired and paid per the employer's terms.
timing: Listings post continuously; optional email alerts push new matches without manual checking.
